Review: The problem is highly relevant to the target study because it directly tests the proposed relationship between spatial coarsening and subharmonic temporal order in the same mechatronic array. It also correctly distinguishes the published claim from what the supplied aggregate export can establish: the export shows time-varying correlation width and shear, but lacks synchronized signals, a direct temporal-order measure, and independent run identifiers. The proposed experiment addresses those limitations with repeated randomized runs, prespecified measurements, and run-level uncertainty.

Feedback: The strongest feature is the causal caution: changing coupling can affect temporal order through pathways other than coarsening, so correlation length is treated as a candidate mediator rather than proof of mechanism. Prespecifying spectral criteria and handling non-onset runs as censored observations should also improve rigor. Clarify how the drive-only comparison isolates direct drive responses, and ensure the chosen temporal-order metric distinguishes genuine subharmonic order from transients, finite-window effects, and frequency drift. Measuring relevant dynamical changes is useful, but avoid treating statistical adjustment for post-treatment variables as sufficient to identify mediation. The question is well scoped to this system; claims about other arrays appropriately remain conditional on further validation.

Rating (1-5): 4
